preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= K for x in stdin.split()[1:K+1])
preconditions.description: The permutation P consists of K integers, each between 1 and K (inclusive), with no duplicates.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.split()) == K + 1 and all(len(line) == K for line in stdin.split()[K+1:])
preconditions.description: The input consists of K+1 lines: first line is K, second line is the permutation P, and the next K lines are K-character strings representing the exchangeability matrix.

preconditions.expression: all(c in 'YN' for line in stdin.split()[K+1:] for c in line)
preconditions.description: Each character in the exchangeability matrix is either 'Y' or 'N'.
The size of the permutation K is less than 101.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= K for x in stdout.split())
postconditions.description: The output is a permutation of K integers, each between 1 and K (inclusive).
The output is a permutation of the original input permutation P.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout.split()[i] <= stdin.split()[1:K+1][j] or (stdin.split()[1:K+1][i] == stdin.split()[1:K+1][j] and i < j) for i in range(K) for j in range(K) if (stdin.split()[K+1+i][j] == 'Y' or i == j))
postconditions.description: For every possible exchangeable pair (i, j) where the exchangeability matrix allows swapping (i.e., matrix[i][j] == 'Y' or i == j), the output permutation is lexicographically smaller than or equal to the permutation obtained by swapping elements i and j in the original permutation P.

postconditions.expression: not any(stdout.split()[i] > stdin.split()[1:K+1][j] and (stdin.split()[K+1+i][j] == 'Y' or i == j) for i in range(K) for j in range(K) if (stdin.split()[1:K+1][i] == stdin.split()[1:K+1][j] and i < j))
postconditions.description: The output permutation is the lexicographically smallest permutation achievable by any sequence of allowed swaps.
